skills.name: Future reference with will and other forms

note.text: Will + base verb can express a prediction, offer or decision, depending on context. Do not add -s or to to the lexical verb after will. Future reference also uses other patterns: be going to for a prior intention or evidence-based prediction, present progressive for an arrangement and simple present for a timetable. These uses overlap in real language. An exercise should specify its intended context rather than mark every alternative future form wrong.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to form will plus a base verb and choose a future expression suited to its context. Builds on: the simple present/past contrast and auxiliary patterns. Leads to: conditional sentences about possible future situations.

sections.heading: Understand the pattern
sections.text: Will + base verb can express a prediction, offer or decision, depending on context. Do not add -s or to to the lexical verb after will. Future reference also uses other patterns: be going to for a prior intention or evidence-based prediction, present progressive for an arrangement and simple present for a timetable. These uses overlap in real language. An exercise should specify its intended context rather than mark every alternative future form wrong.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original dialogue: Bih notices the books on the floor and says, I will help. Ayuk already has a plan: I am going to organise the shelf. Their agreed meeting is tomorrow, while the printed timetable gives a fixed opening time. Each choice presents the future differently; will does not automatically mean a guaranteed fact.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Identify prediction, immediate offer, prior plan, arrangement or timetable. Check the auxiliary and base form. A question with will places it before the subject. Keep the same meaning when correcting the form rather than inventing a new intention.

cards.idea: Distinguish the ideas used in this lesson.
example: will + base verb: a future-reference pattern without an added -s or to.
immediate offer: a willingness to act expressed in response to the situation.
prior intention: a plan already formed before the current exchange.
timetable reference: future reference using a scheduled event.

cards.idea: Read the whole example before identifying its function.
example: Bih will help with the books.
Seeing a difficulty, Bih says I will help.
Ayuk says he is going to organise the shelf he planned to sort.
The printed notice says the room opens tomorrow morning.

cards.idea: A correction must preserve the intended meaning and form.
example: Bih will helps is the standard pattern. Correction: The lexical verb stays in its base form after will.
An immediate offer must always describe a completed past event. Correction: The speaker offers a response at that point.
Every future plan can only be expressed with one form in every context. Correction: Going to is a useful model for the prior intention, without excluding all alternatives.
A present form can never refer to a scheduled future event. Correction: Simple present can describe timetable events.

Will itself forms this negative without does.
